title: AI is automating coding. So why are software developer job postings on the rise?
source_used: UA.NEWS (account of the CNBC story, 11 Oct 2026)
key_facts: US software developer job openings are up nearly 15% since February 2025, when Anthropic launched Claude Code, even as overall job postings fall (CNBC, relayed by UA.NEWS).
Indeed Hiring Lab data shows demand recovering from the 2022 peak but still about 27.5% below the pre-pandemic level.
Senior roles accounted for 71% of the growth in developer postings between May 2025 and May 2026; another 37% of the increase came from roles with AI in the title.
Indeed Hiring Lab economist Sneha Puri said companies need developers to oversee AI output, improve products and help clients adopt new technology.
Stanford's 2026 AI Index: employment of 22-to-25-year-olds in AI-affected occupations fell 16%; for early-career developers the fall was 20%.

GitHub reported that one in three pull requests (proposed code changes) now involves an AI agent, against under one in ten a year earlier, and warned of more vulnerabilities, so human oversight stays necessary.
The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects 10% growth in software developer employment in 2025-2035, from about 1.72 million to 1.89 million jobs.
quote_evidence: In the United States, the number of job openings for software developers has increased by nearly 15% since February 2025, when Anthropic launched Claude Code.
At the same time, the number of job postings for developers is still about 27.5% below its pre-pandemic level.
The bulk of the increase in job openings was in senior and AI-related positions.
why_it_matters_hint: Demand for developers is recovering despite AI coding tools, but the gains go mostly to senior and AI-related roles while beginners face a harder start.
event_date: 11 Oct 2026 (CNBC story); data covers February 2025 to May 2026
